messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: HWE
parts:
Hi Rita,

Technically, from one point of view, testing for deviations from Hardy-Weinberg (HW) proportions is performed at the loci level. However, you could also say that when you estimate FIS (i.e. 1 - (Observed heterozygosity/ Expected heterozygosity under HW equilibrium) you are measuring how much a population is deviating from HW Equilibrium. You can do this by for example typing in the R console:

> res <- gl.report.heterozygosity(platypus.gl)

I recommend reading the following paper:

Waples, R. S. (2015). Testing for Hardy–Weinberg proportions: have we lost the plot?. Journal of heredity, 106(1), 1-19. Link: https://doi.org/10.1093/jhered/esu062

But maybe what you actually want is testing for HW deviations by loci within each population. In that case you can use, for example:

> library(dartR)
> res <- gl.report.hwe(platypus.gl, subset = "each")

You could also have a look to our function gl.diagnostics.hwe which provides you with more insights for HWE issues. 

We also try to provide in the functions' documentation helpful information, and the relevant literature, to help dartR users to solve by themselves this type of questions. 

You can access a function documentation by typing in the R console a question mark followed by the name of the function, for example:

>?gl.report.hwe

You can also have a look to our tutorials if you want to learn more about dartR:

dartR -- R Package for SNP analysis | Georges Lab (biomatix.org)

Cheers,
Luis
